speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy findings of nuclear hyperchromasia and multinucleation are highly suggestive of HPV-related dysplasia or carcinoma. Given the specific involvement of the penis and finger, could you clarify if you have any history of unprotected sexual contact or occupational exposure to potential carcinogens, and have you noticed any inguinal lymphadenopathy?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No known malignancies or hereditary diseases in the family. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema. Social history: Lives with his 4th wife, smokes 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years, has recently immigrated from Africa.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures are classic histological signs of koilocytosis, strongly indicating a high-risk HPV infection. Given the location on the penis and finger, this is consistent with Buschke-Löwenstein tumor (giant condyloma acuminatum) or verrucous carcinoma, which are low-grade but locally aggressive HPV-related lesions. DIAGNOSIS READY: Buschke-Löwenstein tumor
